answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and propagate trust with length-bounded random walks, so influence decays with distance. A Sybil cluster may appear dense internally, like a nebula of mutually reinforcing claims, yet a sparse boundary yields low conductance: few walk transitions cross from trusted nodes. Under a walk-derived voting rule, this bottleneck bounds the cluster’s aggregate weight unless external attestations provide a jetty for trusted signal to enter.
